profiles.name: AI Software & Services
profiles.keywords: artificial intelligence models inference enterprise automation 人工智能
profiles.summary: From computing inputs to models and paid workflows.
profiles.question: Who gets paid when an AI capability becomes a useful workflow?
profiles.scope: Enterprise AI software and services; excludes a standalone valuation of chipmakers or cloud infrastructure.
profiles.geography: Global business-model lens; US framework and vendor examples.

chain.title: Compute & data
chain.actors: Cloud providers, data owners and tooling suppliers
chain.role: Supply the resources used to build and run AI systems.
chain.revenue: Compute consumption, data licensing or tooling contracts.
chain.bottleneck: Can data rights and serving costs support the intended use?

chain.title: Models & deployment
chain.role: Turn resources into usable inference and evaluation services.
chain.revenue: Usage-based APIs, capacity commitments or licenses.
chain.bottleneck: Does reliability hold under real workloads, not just benchmarks?

chain.title: Applications & adoption
chain.actors: Software vendors, integrators and enterprise teams
chain.role: Embed a capability into a customer's operating process.
chain.revenue: Subscriptions, implementation projects or usage fees.
chain.bottleneck: Will verified savings translate into repeat paid use?

profiles.economics: Follow customer revenue after inference, support and integration costs. A growing user count alone does not establish attractive unit economics.
drivers: Which workflows have measurable time savings?
Do pilots become recurring paid deployments?
risks: Model errors, data rights and accountability may block adoption.
Falling model prices may help customers without improving every supplier's margin.

metrics.name: Cost per completed task
metrics.meaning: Include inference, retries and human review; compare like-for-like tasks.

metrics.name: Paid retention
metrics.meaning: Track continued paid use, not registrations or free trials.

metrics.name: Task success rate
metrics.meaning: Use a defined test set and disclose human intervention.

evidence.text: Amazon Bedrock publishes input/output token pricing for several models, providing a concrete example of usage-based inference billing.
NIST's AI RMF is voluntary guidance for managing risk across AI design, development, use and evaluation.

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock Pricing
sources.supports: Billing-model example only; no price or market-size estimate is reproduced.

sources.title: AI Risk Management Framework
sources.supports: Risk-management scope; not a revenue forecast or an official value-chain taxonomy.

profiles.name: Semiconductors
profiles.keywords: chips integrated circuits foundry design packaging 半导体 芯片
profiles.summary: From chip design to fabrication, packaging and testing.
profiles.question: Which production constraint determines where value is captured?
profiles.scope: Semiconductor production, with equipment and materials as enabling inputs. Not a ranking of individual companies or process nodes.

chain.title: Design
chain.role: Specify the device and prepare it for production.
chain.revenue: Chip sales, design services or intellectual-property licensing.
chain.bottleneck: Can the design meet performance, power and cost requirements?

chain.title: Wafer fabrication
chain.actors: Foundries, integrated manufacturers and input suppliers
chain.role: Fabricate circuits on wafers using specialized facilities.
chain.revenue: Manufacturing services or internally produced chip sales.
chain.bottleneck: Are yield and utilization sufficient to cover fixed costs?

chain.title: Assembly, test & packaging
chain.role: Separate, test and package devices for customers.
chain.revenue: Packaging and testing services or bundled chip sales.
chain.bottleneck: Can packaging capacity and reliability meet product requirements?

profiles.economics: Separate design economics from capital-intensive manufacturing. A shortage in one process or package does not imply a shortage across all chips.
drivers: Which applications are creating durable design wins?
Where do customer requirements exceed available production capability?
risks: Capacity additions can arrive after the demand cycle changes.
Geographic dependencies and customer concentration require separate analysis.

metrics.name: Manufacturing yield
metrics.meaning: Good devices as a share of output, for a specified product/process.

metrics.name: Capacity utilization
metrics.meaning: Track actual loading, not announced capacity alone.

metrics.name: Inventory & lead time
metrics.meaning: Read together to distinguish shortages from order inflation.

evidence.text: SIA's primer distinguishes design, front-end fabrication and back-end assembly, test and packaging. The three-stage map here follows that production sequence.

sources.title: Semiconductor Industry Primer: The Stages of Production and Business Models
sources.supports: Production stages; foundational reference, not current market sizing.

profiles.name: Batteries & Energy Storage
profiles.keywords: battery lithium stationary grid minerals cells 储能 电池
profiles.summary: From minerals and cells to installed storage systems.
profiles.question: Who earns the return: material suppliers, manufacturers or operators?
profiles.scope: Battery supply chains, with a stationary-storage operating lens. EV batteries and grid-storage revenue pools are not interchangeable.
profiles.geography: Global supply chain; project economics depend on local power markets.

chain.title: Materials & components
chain.revenue: Material and component sales under spot or contract terms.
chain.bottleneck: Do quality, supply security and chemistry choices align?

chain.title: Cells & systems
chain.actors: Cell makers, pack makers and system integrators
chain.role: Turn components into a tested, controllable storage system.
chain.revenue: Cell/system sales, integration and warranty services.
chain.bottleneck: Can manufacturing quality and warranty obligations be sustained?

chain.title: Projects & operation
chain.role: Connect and operate assets to serve a particular power market.
chain.bottleneck: Will local revenues cover degradation and full project costs?

profiles.economics: Do not equate cheaper cells with better project returns. Connection, installation, financing, degradation and market rules belong in the same model.
drivers: Where does variable generation create a need for flexibility?
Can storage participate and get paid in the relevant local market?
risks: Safety, degradation and warranties may change lifecycle costs.
Supply concentration and changing project revenues can offset lower hardware prices.

metrics.name: Installed system cost
metrics.meaning: Use consistent currency, date and system boundary; distinguish USD/kW from USD/kWh.

metrics.name: Usable capacity & efficiency
metrics.meaning: Measure at the same operating conditions and asset age.

metrics.name: Contracted revenue share
metrics.meaning: Separate contracted cash flows from merchant assumptions.

evidence.text: The IEA describes concentration across battery supply chains and explains storage's role in flexibility and grid stability. Its 2024 scenarios are not treated here as current forecasts.

sources.title: Batteries and Secure Energy Transitions — Executive summary
sources.supports: Supply-chain structure and power-system applications; historical scenarios, not fresh market estimates.

profiles.name: Cybersecurity
profiles.keywords: security identity threat intelligence detection response 网络安全
profiles.summary: From security inputs to products and operational response.
profiles.question: Does the customer buy another tool, or a better security outcome?
profiles.scope: Enterprise security products and services. The commercial layers below are DEX's map, not the NIST CSF functions or a compliance checklist.
profiles.geography: Global enterprise lens; NIST provides the risk-management reference.

chain.title: Signals & foundations
chain.role: Supply the information and controls used by security teams.
chain.revenue: Data feeds, infrastructure or identity-service contracts.
chain.bottleneck: Are the signals relevant, complete and lawful to use?

chain.title: Security products
chain.actors: Endpoint, cloud, network and identity vendors
chain.role: Turn inputs into prevention, detection and investigation tools.
chain.bottleneck: Can tools integrate without overwhelming operators?

chain.title: Operations & response
chain.actors: Internal teams, managed providers and responders
chain.role: Operate controls and coordinate incident handling and recovery.
chain.revenue: Managed-service contracts, retainers or response projects.
chain.bottleneck: Can the customer turn alerts into timely, effective action?

profiles.economics: Test renewal quality and delivery cost alongside product claims. Security spending is not itself evidence that customer risk has fallen.
drivers: Which assets and workflows create an uncovered exposure?
Would integration or managed delivery solve a staffing bottleneck?
risks: Product overlap and tool consolidation may affect renewals.
Failures in the vendor's own systems can undermine trust.

metrics.name: Net revenue retention
metrics.meaning: Use a consistent cohort and vendor definition.

metrics.name: Response effectiveness
metrics.meaning: Define incident severity and measurement boundaries before comparing.

metrics.name: Service delivery cost
metrics.meaning: Include analyst time and infrastructure per customer.

evidence.text: NIST CSF 2.0 organizes cybersecurity outcomes under Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover. These are outcomes, not six sequential commercial stages.

sources.title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
sources.supports: Risk-management functions only; does not establish vendor revenue, effectiveness or market size.

profiles.name: Robotics
profiles.keywords: robots automation industrial integration actuators cobots 机器人
profiles.summary: From components to integrated, supported automation.
profiles.question: Can a robot deliver a repeatable outcome in a real operating environment?
profiles.scope: Industrial robot systems and their integration. This is a subset of the explorer's Industrial + Service Robotics row; not a humanoid or service-robot forecast.
profiles.geography: Global industrial lens; ABB is one vendor example, not a market ranking.

chain.title: Components & control
chain.role: Provide the hardware and software building blocks.
chain.bottleneck: Can parts satisfy precision, durability and integration requirements?

chain.title: Robots & integration
chain.role: Combine machines, tooling and software around a defined task.
chain.bottleneck: How much customization is required for each deployment?

chain.title: Operation & lifecycle
chain.role: Commission, maintain and improve the deployed system.
chain.bottleneck: Does uptime and throughput justify the full lifecycle cost?

profiles.economics: Evaluate the complete installed cell and support burden, not just the robot's purchase price. Pilot demonstrations are not recurring production deployments.
drivers: Which repetitive tasks have stable requirements and measurable payback?
Can integration be reused across multiple customer sites?
risks: Customization and commissioning delays can erode project margins.
Reliability, operator training and safe integration need on-site validation.

metrics.name: Installed-system payback
metrics.meaning: Include integration, downtime, maintenance and training.

metrics.name: Productive uptime
metrics.meaning: Measure time actually completing the intended task.

metrics.name: Repeat deployments
metrics.meaning: Separate pilots from repeat orders and operating installations.

evidence.text: ABB's robotics services cover installation, support, maintenance and modernization, illustrating commercial activity beyond the initial equipment sale.

sources.title: Robotics Services
sources.supports: One vendor's service offerings; not independent evidence of achieved returns or industry-wide revenue mix.

profiles.name: Biopharmaceuticals
profiles.keywords: biotech pharmaceuticals drugs clinical trials medicine 生物制药 医药
profiles.summary: From scientific discovery to evidence and commercialization.
profiles.question: How does a scientific asset become an approved and commercially viable product?
profiles.scope: Innovative drug development. The US pathway is an illustrative regulatory reference; individual products and other jurisdictions require separate analysis.
profiles.geography: US regulatory reference; not a universal approval pathway.

chain.title: Discovery & preclinical
chain.actors: Research teams, biotechs and research suppliers
chain.role: Develop candidates and investigate their properties before human studies.
chain.revenue: Research services or licensing arrangements to investigate.
chain.bottleneck: Does the evidence justify further development and funding?

chain.title: Clinical evidence & review
chain.role: Generate human evidence and evaluate a submission for approval.
chain.revenue: Trial-service contracts or milestone arrangements to investigate.
chain.bottleneck: Are safety, efficacy and manufacturing evidence sufficient?

chain.title: Manufacture & access
chain.actors: Manufacturers, commercial teams and health-system buyers
chain.role: Supply approved products while maintaining quality and safety monitoring.
chain.revenue: Product sales, royalties or manufacturing services to investigate.
chain.bottleneck: Does approval translate into supply, access and viable net revenue?

profiles.economics: Separate scientific progress, approval and commercial success. Model development spending and potential dilution before assuming future product revenue.
drivers: What unmet need would a successful product address?
Which evidence would change clinical or purchasing decisions?
risks: Clinical failure and manufacturing problems can change the entire thesis.
Approval alone does not establish reimbursement or commercial demand.

metrics.name: Evidence milestones
metrics.meaning: State trial phase, population and endpoints; avoid treating a milestone as guaranteed.

metrics.name: Cash runway
metrics.meaning: Test spending assumptions and funding needs under delays.

metrics.name: Net realized revenue
metrics.meaning: Distinguish actual sales from headline prices and potential markets.

evidence.text: FDA's drug-development overview describes discovery, preclinical research, clinical research, review and post-market safety monitoring. The three cards group those activities for readability.

sources.title: The Drug Development Process
sources.published: Undated overview; reviewed on the date shown above
sources.supports: US development and review stages; not clinical advice or evidence for a particular drug.
